**Subject: Offer of Employment — Senior Electrical Design Engineer**

Dear Meera,

Further to your application and the subsequent interview rounds, we are delighted to offer you employment with Solara Renewables ("the Company") in the position of Senior Electrical Design Engineer, within the R&D & Engineering function, reporting to Ms. Sanjana Kulkarni, Vice President & Head of R&D. We were impressed by your experience in power-electronics design and are confident you will make a strong contribution to our string-inverter platform.

The key terms of this offer are set out below. Detailed terms will follow in your Employment Contract, to be issued and countersigned on or before your date of joining.

## **1. Position and Reporting**

Designation: Senior Electrical Design Engineer (Grade M2)

Function: R&D & Engineering

Reporting Manager: Ms. Sanjana Kulkarni, Vice President & Head of R&D (CTO)

Work Location: Corporate Office, 7th Floor, Cybercity Business Hub, Viman Nagar, Pune - 411014, with periodic travel to Plant 1 (Chakan) for design validation and pilot builds.

## **2. Date of Joining**

Your date of joining will be 15 September 2026. Please report to the Human Resources & Admin desk, Corporate Office, at 9:00 AM on this date. If this date is not convenient, please inform Talent Acquisition (careers@solararenewables.in) at the earliest so an alternative can be discussed; this offer is contingent on joining within 30 days of the date of this letter.

## **3. Compensation**

Your Cost to Company (CTC) will be ₹14,40,000 (Rupees Fourteen Lakh Forty Thousand only) per annum, structured per the break-up at Annexure A. This is inclusive of statutory employer contributions (Provident Fund, Gratuity) and the variable pay component. Compensation will be reviewed annually as part of the Company's performance and compensation review cycle, ordinarily each April, though such a review does not guarantee an increase.

## **4. Employment Type and Probation**

This is a full-time, permanent position. You will be on probation for the first 6 (six) months from your date of joining, during which either party may terminate this employment by giving 15 (fifteen) days' written notice, or payment in lieu thereof. Your employment will be confirmed in writing on satisfactory completion of probation, based on a formal review with your Reporting Manager and Human Resources.

## **5. Notice Period (Post-Confirmation)**

Following confirmation, either party may terminate the employment by giving 60 (sixty) days' written notice, or the Company may pay salary in lieu of the unserved notice period, at its discretion.

## **6. Conditions of this Offer**

- Satisfactory completion of background verification (education, prior employment, address and criminal record check) conducted through the Company's empanelled agency.
- Submission of original documents for verification as listed in Annexure B, on or before your date of joining.
- Confirmation that you are not bound by any restrictive covenant (notice period, non-compete, or garden leave) with your current or previous employer that would prevent you from joining on the proposed date.
- A satisfactory medical fitness declaration, where applicable to your role.

This offer stands withdrawn if any of the above conditions is not satisfactorily met, or if any information provided by you during the recruitment process is found to be false or materially misleading, whether discovered before or after your date of joining.

## **7. Confidentiality**

The terms of this offer are confidential and personal to you. Please do not disclose the contents of this letter to other employees or external parties, other than to your immediate family or professional advisors as needed.

## **8. Acceptance**

Please indicate your acceptance of this offer by signing and returning the enclosed duplicate of this letter within 5 (five) working days of the date above. We look forward to welcoming you to the Solara Renewables team.

Yours sincerely,

For Solara Renewables & Manufacturing Private Limited

Ananya Rao

Vice President, People & Culture

# EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Employment Agreement ("Agreement") is made and entered into at Pune on this 10th day of September, 2026 BETWEEN Solara Renewables & Manufacturing Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at Plot No. 42, MIDC Industrial Area, Chakan, Pune - 410501, Maharashtra, India (hereinafter referred to as "the Company", which expression shall unless repugnant to the context include its successors and permitted assigns), of the ONE PART; AND Ms. Meera Joshi, D/o Mr. Prakash Joshi, residing at A-12, Prabhat Residency, Kothrud, Pune - 411038 (hereinafter referred to as "the Employee") of the OTHER PART. The Company and the Employee are hereinafter individually referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".

## 1. Appointment and Designation

1.1 The Company hereby appoints the Employee, and the Employee accepts such appointment, as Senior Electrical Design Engineer (Grade M2) in the R&D & Engineering function, on the terms and conditions set out in this Agreement and in the Company's HR policies as amended from time to time.
1.2 The Employee's date of joining and effective date of this Agreement is 15 September 2026 ("Effective Date"). The Employee's Employee Code is SOL-EMP-0288.
1.3 The Employee will report to the Vice President & Head of R&D, or such other person as the Company may designate from time to time.
## 2. Probation and Confirmation

2.1 The Employee shall be on probation for a period of 6 (six) months from the Effective Date.
2.2 During probation, either Party may terminate this Agreement by giving 15 (fifteen) days' prior written notice, or payment in lieu thereof, without assigning any reason.
2.3 The Company may, at its sole discretion, extend the probation period by up to 3 (three) additional months where performance during the initial period has been inconclusive, with reasons communicated in writing.
2.4 On satisfactory completion of probation, the Company shall issue a written confirmation of employment.

### 1. Welcome to Solara Renewables

On behalf of the leadership team, welcome to Solara Renewables. Since our founding in March 2014, we have grown from a small design team in Pune into a company of 287+ people designing and manufacturing solar string inverters and mounting structures for commercial and industrial customers across India. This handbook is a practical guide to how we work together — our policies, your entitlements, and the standards we hold ourselves to. It is not a contract of employment; your Employment Contract and applicable law take precedence in the event of any conflict. Policies in this handbook may be updated from time to time, and the current version is always available on the Company intranet (SolaraConnect).

#### 1.1 Our Business

Solara Renewables designs, manufactures and provides EPC support for solar string inverters and rooftop/ground-mount structures, serving commercial and industrial (C&I) solar developers and EPC contractors. We operate two manufacturing plants in the Pune district (Chakan and Ranjangaon), a corporate office in Viman Nagar, Pune, and a sales office in Bengaluru.

#### 1.2 Our Values

- Engineering Integrity — we design and build to last; we do not cut corners on safety or quality.
- Ownership — we take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.
- Respect — we treat colleagues, customers, and partners with courtesy and fairness.
- Speed with Discipline — we move quickly, but within process and safety guardrails.

### 2. Employment Basics

#### 2.1 Employment Types

The Company engages employees under the following categories, each governed by the terms of the individual's Employment Contract:

- Full-time, Permanent — the standard employment category for most roles.
- Full-time, Probationary — new joiners, for the duration of their probation period (typically 3-6 months depending on grade).
- Fixed-Term Contract — for defined project-based or seasonal requirements.
#### 2.2 Working Hours

Standard working hours for corporate office roles are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday to Friday, with a 1-hour lunch break. Plant-based roles follow shift schedules (General Shift, Shift A 6:00 AM-2:00 PM, Shift B 2:00 PM-10:00 PM) as notified by the Plant HR team. Employees are expected to record attendance via the biometric system at the plants or the HRIS check-in for corporate/sales office roles.

#### 2.3 Probation and Confirmation

New joiners are typically on probation for 3-6 months depending on grade, as specified in their Employment Contract. Confirmation is based on a formal review between the employee and their Reporting Manager, coordinated by HR, and is not automatic on completion of the probation period.

#### 2.4 Attendance and Punctuality

Employees are expected to be punctual and to record attendance accurately. Persistent unexplained absence or late attendance may be addressed through the counselling and disciplinary process described in Section 13.

#### 2.5 Identity Cards and Access

All employees are issued a photo identity card and, where applicable, an access card for plant or office entry. These must be worn visibly at all times on Company premises and returned to Admin/HR on separation.

### 3. Code of Conduct & Ethics

Every employee is expected to act with honesty, fairness, and professionalism in all dealings with colleagues, customers, suppliers, and the public.

#### 3.1 General Conduct

- Treat all colleagues, customers, and visitors with courtesy and respect, regardless of role, background, or seniority.
- Avoid conduct that creates a hostile, offensive, or unsafe work environment.
- Maintain confidentiality of Company, customer, and colleague information.
- Use Company assets (equipment, vehicles, IT systems) responsibly and for legitimate business purposes.
#### 3.2 Conflict of Interest

Employees must disclose to HR and their Reporting Manager any situation that could reasonably create a conflict of interest — for example, a financial interest in a supplier or customer, or a close personal relationship with someone in their reporting line. Undisclosed conflicts of interest may be treated as a disciplinary matter.

#### 3.3 Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption

Employees must not offer, give, solicit, or accept any bribe, kickback, or improper payment in connection with Company business. Gifts and hospitality from suppliers or customers beyond nominal, customary value must be declined or reported to HR/Compliance.

#### 3.4 Gifts, Entertainment, and Vendor Relations

Modest, occasional gifts of nominal value (below 2,500) customary to business relationships may be ₹ accepted; anything beyond this threshold must be declined, returned, or, where declining would cause offence, surrendered to HR and logged in the Gift Register.

#### 3.5 Use of Social Media

Employees are free to participate in social media in a personal capacity but must not disclose confidential Company information, speak on the Company's behalf without authorisation, or post content that could bring the Company into disrepute.

### 4. Anti-Harassment & Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy

Solara Renewables is committed to providing a safe workplace, free from sexual harassment, in compliance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 ("POSH Act").

#### 4.1 What Constitutes Sexual Harassment

Sexual harassment includes unwelcome sexually determined behaviour, whether directly or by implication, including: physical contact and advances; demand or request for sexual favours; sexually coloured remarks; showing pornography; or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

#### 4.2 Internal Committee (IC)

The Company has constituted an Internal Committee under the POSH Act to receive and inquire into complaints. The current IC composition, presiding officer, and contact details are published on SolaraConnect and displayed at all office and plant locations. See the separate 'POSH Compliance Committee — Constitution & Annual Report' document for full details, including the external member and reporting statistics.

#### 4.3 How to Report

A complaint may be made in writing to the Internal Committee within 3 months of the incident (extendable at the Committee's discretion). Complaints may be submitted via email to icc@solararenewables.in, in a sealed letter to the IC Presiding Officer, or verbally to any IC member, who will assist in recording it in writing.

#### 4.4 Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation

The identity of the complainant, respondent, and witnesses will be kept confidential throughout the process, to the extent permitted by law. Retaliation against a complainant or witness is strictly prohibited and will itself be treated as a serious disciplinary matter.

#### 4.5 Process and Timelines

The IC will complete its inquiry within 90 days of receiving a complaint and submit its report and recommendations to the Company, which must act on the recommendations within 60 days, per the POSH Act.

### 5. Compensation & Benefits

#### 5.1 Salary Structure and Payment

Salaries are paid monthly, credited to the employee's registered bank account by the 1st working day of the following month. Payslips are available through the HRIS employee self-service portal.

#### 5.2 Statutory Benefits

- Provident Fund (PF): 12% of Basic Salary contributed by both employee and employer, per the EPF Act, 1952 (subject to the statutory wage ceiling).
- Gratuity: payable per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, to employees who complete 5 years of continuous service.
- Employees' State Insurance (ESIC): applicable to employees with gross monthly wages up to the statutory threshold, currently 21,000. ₹
- Professional Tax: deducted per the applicable state slab (Maharashtra).
#### 5.3 Group Insurance Benefits

- Group Mediclaim Insurance: covering the employee, spouse, and up to 2 dependent children, with a base sum insured of 3,00,000 (enhanceable via voluntary top-up at employee cost). ₹
- Group Personal Accident Insurance: sum insured of 3x annual CTC (subject to policy caps).
- Group Term Life Insurance: sum insured of 2x annual CTC.
#### 5.4 Other Benefits

- Meal card / subsidised canteen at plant locations.
- Transport facility (bus/shuttle) between designated pickup points and Plant 1/Plant 2.
- Mobile and internet reimbursement for eligible grades (M1 and above), per the Travel & Expense Policy.
- Annual health check-up for employees at grade M1 and above, and for all plant-based employees per statutory requirements.

### 6. Leave Policy

#### 6.1 Applying for Leave

Leave must be applied for in advance through the HRIS Leave Management Module, except in cases of medical emergency, where the employee (or a family member) should inform the Reporting Manager as soon as reasonably possible and regularise the application on return.

#### 6.2 Public Holidays

The Company observes 10-12 public holidays each calendar year, notified in December for the following year, including national holidays (Republic Day, Independence Day, Gandhi Jayanti) and regionally observed festivals.

### 7. Health, Safety & Environment (EHS)

Safety is a shared responsibility. All employees, particularly those working at Plant 1 and Plant 2, must comply with EHS protocols at all times.

#### 7.1 General Safety Requirements

- Wear the prescribed Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in designated areas at all times (safety shoes, safety glasses, ESD wrist straps in electronics assembly areas).
- Follow Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures before servicing or clearing jams on any powered equipment.
- Report any unsafe condition, near-miss, or incident to your supervisor and the EHS team immediately, using the Incident Report Form on SolaraConnect.
- Participate in mandatory fire safety and evacuation drills, conducted at least twice a year at each plant.
#### 7.2 Incident Reporting and Investigation

All incidents, including near-misses, must be reported within 24 hours. The EHS team will investigate incidents resulting in injury or significant property damage and issue a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) report within 7 working days.

#### 7.3 Environmental Compliance

The Company is committed to responsible handling and disposal of electronic waste, packaging materials, and hazardous substances (e.g., solder, cleaning agents) per applicable Pollution Control Board norms. Employees handling such materials must follow the plant's Waste Management SOP.

### 8. Information Technology & Information Security Policy

#### 8.1 Acceptable Use

Company IT assets (laptops, email, network access) are provided for business use. Limited, reasonable personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with work, consume excessive resources, or violate this policy.

#### 8.2 Password and Access Management

- Use strong, unique passwords for Company systems and enable multi-factor authentication where offered.
- Never share login credentials with anyone, including colleagues or IT support staff.
- Lock your workstation when unattended.
#### 8.3 Data Protection and Confidentiality

Employees must not store Company confidential data (customer data, design files, financial data) on personal devices or unauthorised cloud storage. All confidential data must be handled per its classification (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) as defined in the Information Classification Standard.

#### 8.4 Incident Reporting

Suspected phishing emails, lost/stolen devices, or any suspected security incident must be reported immediately to IT Security at itsecurity@solararenewables.in.

#### 8.5 Software and Licensing

Only Company-approved and licensed software may be installed on Company devices. Installation of unauthorised or pirated software is a disciplinary matter.

### 9. Learning & Development

The Company invests in employee growth through structured training, certifications, and on-the-job development.

#### 9.1 Mandatory Training

All employees must complete the following within the timelines specified: POSH Awareness Training (within 30 days of joining, annually thereafter), Information Security Awareness (within 30 days of joining, annually thereafter), and role-specific safety training for plant-based roles (before working unsupervised on the shop floor).

#### 9.2 Skill Development Support

Employees may request sponsorship for relevant external certifications and training programs through their Reporting Manager, subject to budget approval and a minimum post-training service commitment for programs above 50,000 in cost. ₹

#### 9.3 Internal Mobility

Employees who have completed 18 months in their current role and are in good standing may apply for internally posted openings through the Internal Job Posting (IJP) process on SolaraConnect.

### 10. Performance Management

The Company follows an annual performance management cycle aligned to the fiscal year (April-March), comprising goal-setting, a mid-year check-in, and a year-end review.

#### 10.1 Goal Setting

Goals are set within the first 6 weeks of the fiscal year, aligned to team and company objectives, and documented in the Performance Management module of the HRIS.

#### 10.2 Mid-Year and Year-End Reviews

Managers and employees conduct a documented mid-year check-in (typically October) and a formal year- end review (typically March-April), covering goal achievement, competencies, and development areas. See the separate Performance Review template for the full form.

### 12. Grievance Redressal

Employees who have a work-related grievance (other than sexual harassment complaints, which follow the POSH process in Section 4) are encouraged to raise it promptly through the following escalation path:

1. Discuss informally with your immediate Reporting Manager.
2. If unresolved within 7 working days, escalate in writing to your Department Head, copying HR.
3. If still unresolved, escalate to the Senior Manager-HR (Employee Relations & Compliance), who will investigate and respond within 15 working days.
4. Grievances relating to compensation, promotion, or performance ratings may additionally be raised through the annual Calibration Appeal window, communicated by HR at the close of each review cycle.
All grievances will be handled confidentially, and employees will not face retaliation for raising a grievance in good faith.

### 13. Disciplinary Policy

The Company follows a principle of progressive discipline for performance and conduct issues, except in cases of gross misconduct, which may warrant immediate action.

#### 13.1 Examples of Misconduct

- Minor: repeated unpunctuality, unauthorised absence, non-compliance with dress code or minor SOP deviations.
- Major: insubordination, harassment, breach of confidentiality, conflict of interest non-disclosure, repeated policy violations after warning.
- Gross: theft, fraud, violence, being under the influence of alcohol/drugs at work, serious safety violations, sexual harassment (handled under the POSH Policy).
#### 13.2 Process

5. Verbal counselling and documentation for minor first instances.
6. Written warning for repeated or moderate issues, with a copy filed in the employee's HR record.
7. Show-cause notice and inquiry for major/gross misconduct, with the employee given an opportunity to respond, and may include suspension pending inquiry (with subsistence allowance per the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, where applicable).
8. Final action — ranging from final written warning, to termination — based on the inquiry findings, approved by HR and the relevant Department Head.

Dear All,

Following feedback gathered through the Q3 Employee Engagement Survey and consultation with department heads, we are updating two related policies effective 1 October 2026. Please read this memo carefully — it supersedes Sections 2.2 and 5.4 of the Employee Handbook (Version 4.2) until the next full handbook revision incorporates these changes.

## 1. What is Changing

- Hybrid Work Eligibility: Corporate-office employees at grade E4 and above, whose roles do not require daily physical presence (confirmed by their department head), may work from home up to 2 days per week, subject to manager approval and core-hours availability (10:00 AM-4:00 PM) for meetings.
- Mobile & Internet Reimbursement: The eligibility threshold is being lowered from grade M1 to grade E4 and above, and the monthly cap is being raised from 1,500 to 1,800, reflecting current market ₹ ₹ rates for broadband and mobile data plans.
- Plant-based and field-based roles (Manufacturing, QA, Supply Chain warehouse staff) are not eligible for hybrid work under this policy, given the nature of on-site work; this is unchanged from the existing policy.
## 2. Why We're Making This Change

41% of respondents to the Q3 engagement survey specifically flagged commute and flexibility as an area for improvement, and several department heads separately raised that the existing M1+ threshold for reimbursement excluded several E3/E4 employees who are now regularly using personal data plans for work calls and email outside office hours. This update responds directly to both points.

## 3. What You Need to Do

1. If you are grade E4 or above in a corporate-office role, discuss hybrid-work eligibility and your preferred WFH days with your Reporting Manager by 20 September 2026.
2. Approved hybrid arrangements must be logged in the HRIS Attendance module so plant/office access and headcount planning remain accurate.
3. If you are newly eligible for mobile/internet reimbursement (grade E4), submit your first claim through the existing Expense Module from 1 October 2026 onward; no separate registration is required.
4. Managers: please flag any role that you believe should be hybrid-eligible but sits below E4, or vice versa, to HR by 15 September 2026 for review — this is a policy floor, not a rigid rule, and we expect a small number of exceptions.
